Use a set of identifiers for the duration of a call

Source: R/identifiers_scope.R
local_identifiers.Rd

local_identifiers() makes ids the active identifiers until the calling function returns, on success or on error, then restores the identifiers that were active before. with_identifiers() does the same around one expression, and with_SE_identifiers() uses the identifiers stored on a SummarizedExperiment. Keys absent from ids keep their current value.

Usage

local_identifiers(ids, .local_envir = parent.frame())

with_identifiers(ids, code)

with_SE_identifiers(se, code)

Arguments

ids

named list of identifiers, a subset of names(get_default_identifiers()).

.local_envir

environment whose exit restores the previous identifiers.

code

expression evaluated with the identifiers active.

se

a SummarizedExperiment.

Value

local_identifiers(): the identifiers active before, invisibly. with_identifiers() and with_SE_identifiers(): the value of code.

Details

Prefer these to set_env_identifier(), which changes the identifiers for the rest of the session. Called at the top level (the console), there is no function to return from, so local_identifiers() warns and the identifiers stay set, as with set_env_identifier().

An SE built by gDRcore stores the identifiers it was built with, and the functions that read an SE (convert_se_assay_to_dt(), validate_SE(), apply_fit(), ...) use them in preference to the session's. A key the SE does not store is taken from the session, as get_SE_identifiers() always did. To correct an object's identifiers, use set_SE_identifiers().

Examples

f <- function() {
  local_identifiers(list(drug = "DrugID"))
  get_env_identifiers("drug")
}
f()                         # "DrugID"
#> [1] "DrugID"
get_env_identifiers("drug") # unchanged
#> [1] "Gnumber"
with_identifiers(list(cellline = "Clid"), get_env_identifiers("cellline"))
#> [1] "Clid"
